rubric_source: user-supplied v0.2 Alpha Human Adjudication Rubric

labels.adjudication_reason: Bullish analyst sentiment and a price target state an outcome/opinion but no canonical Alpha mechanism or underlying driver.
The claim explicitly states accelerating revenue growth and an 85% YoY increase, directly engaging Revenue Expansion.
Record revenue is the most direct canonical mechanism in the mixed financial/technical statement; the valuation figures are not themselves framed as rich-valuation downside risk.
A Bollinger-band resistance level is a technical level and does not substantively engage any canonical Alpha thesis.
A strong operating margin is a profitability metric, not by itself a demand/revenue, AI, cycle, valuation-compression, macro, or narrative mechanism.
The claim explicitly argues that growth is insufficient to justify a 19x price-to-sales multiple, directly expressing rich-valuation downside risk.
The claim describes a specific expected $14B revenue contribution from a product, directly engaging a revenue-expansion mechanism.
ROA is a profitability/efficiency metric and does not directly instantiate any canonical Alpha mechanism.
A standalone forward-EPS figure is a bare metric without a revision, demand driver, or other canonical mechanism.
Saying a generic fundamental bull case was not refuted gives no concrete driver or mechanism for any canonical Alpha.
High switching costs between foundries describe competitive stickiness, which is not one of the canonical Alpha mechanisms.
Low probabilities of reaching revenue thresholds express skepticism about an outcome but do not positively instantiate a canonical Alpha thesis; no alternative canonical mechanism is asserted.
RSI neutralization is a technical-momentum observation, not a canonical Alpha mechanism.
Earnings-quality distortion from investment gains is an accounting-quality issue not represented by the canonical Alpha taxonomy.

The statement calls AI strategy a growth driver but does not describe training/adoption-driven accelerator demand, inference demand, or AI-infrastructure buildout; the AI mention alone is insufficient.

The statement describes a downside scenario in which AI-capex cuts lead to slower revenue growth; under the rubric this is a negation/invalidation path rather than a positive instance of a single canonical Alpha thesis.
